description.narrative: The development objective of the Second Science and Technology Project is to support Croatia to absorb European Union (EU) funds in the research and innovation sector by capacitating selected public sector organizations and stimulating the demand for those funds from the business and scientific communities. There are two components to the project. The first component of the project is capacity building for absorption of EU funds. This component will provide technical assistance primarily to the Ministry of Science, Education and Sports (MSES), Unity through Knowledge Fund (UKF) and Business Innovation Croatian Agency (BICRO), and other organizations may be considered based on needs analysis. It consists of three types of activities. The second of the project is research and innovation programs. This component will finance programs previously supported by Science and Technology Project (STP), through MSES, BICRO and UKF, in order to maintain and increase the pool of Small and Medium Enterprise (SMEs) and researchers that could apply to future EU-financed grant schemes. A detailed review of the projects financed under the STP will be performed and the results of this review will be taken into account in the preparation of the future calls.

The development objective of the proposed Project is to support Croatia to absorb EU Funds in the research and innovation sector bycapacitating selected public sector organizations and stimulating the demand for those funds from the business and scientific communities.

title.narrative: Total value of projects in the pipeline for funding by EU Funds originated from UKF funded projects (in million Euro)

comment.narrative:
<p>Surpassed. Indicator was revised in April 2017. The end target was increased from EUR1.6 million to EUR24 million and the description of the indicator was clarified to reflect the impact of the actual allocation of funds per programs. The gap between the initial and revised end-target and the achieved value is due to a cautiously set indicator at the appraisal - based on previous poor absorption of the EU's R&D Framework Programs of Croatia's science, early lessons from STP and the lack of information about upcoming ESIF programs. As soon as the established researchers among UKF beneficiaries (under the Cooperability Program) demonstrated their ability to be awarded the EU's Horizon 2020 funds and prepared initial applications to newly launched ESIF in Croatia, the end-target was increased through restructuring.</p>

<p>The significant over-achievement of this indicator reflects a remarkable quality of the projects selected for UKF financing. The value includes the project pipeline developed as a result of implemented UKF projects, of which some have already been awarded EU funding. There are three main types of project proposals developed depending on financing resources:</p>

<p>1. HORIZON 2020 and other European central programs, notably the ERC (European Research Council), Marie Curie funds, FET (Future and Emerging Technologies), Erasmus, FLAG-ERA Consortium, bilateral projects); these amount in total to EUR­­44.29 million. Since 2007, only six ERC projects, which are the most prestigious in Europe, were awarded to Croatian researchers, out of which three went to UKF researchers based on the outstanding results and collaboration established under UKF.</p>

<p>2. INTERREG are programs of European Territorial Cooperation (ETC) under which the UKF beneficiaries generated the projects in the value of EUR5.81 million;</p>

<p>3. European and Structural Investment Funds (ESIF) under two programs: Operational Programme Competitiveness and Cohesion (OPCC) 2014-2020 and Operational Programme Effective Human Resources (OPEHR) 2014-2020. The value of the project pipeline under ESIF amounts to EUR16.21 million and refers to grant awards under Centers of Excellence and infrastructure projects under OPCC as well as under the OPEHR funds for post-doctoral projects.</p>

<p>As of end-April 2020, of total EUR66.32million worth pipeline, EUR22.65 million were already awarded and are in implementation. Finally, additional EUR5.6 million worth projects were developed for financing from other international sources.</p>

<p>The indicator refers to the number of items achieved (it does not include planned IPR). The share of IPR products/processes by programs are as follows:</p>

comment.narrative:
<p>End target revised in April 201, and again in October 2018. Indicator surpassed. Total number of contracted projects:</p>

<p>40 PoC (Call #4); 49 PoC (Call #5); 62 PoC (Call #6); 54 PoC (Call #7); 9 RAZUM projects; 21 IRCRO projects; and 15 projects under the Technology Transfer Support Program.</p>

<p>The government has continued to finance the PoC program for the private sector and undr its Call #8 - 83 projects have been contracted, worth EUR4.4 million, which have been in implementation since December 2019.</p>

title.narrative: Number of trained staff in the MSES and its organizations and R&D institutions (e.g. HAMAG-BICRO, UKF, TTOs, CSF) on EU procedures for project preparation and implementation

comment.narrative: <p> Indicator exceeded. Training provided to the staff in key R&D institutions had positively affected the capacity of the research and innovation stakeholders to use and manage EU funds in several ways: (a) HAMAG-BICRO serves as an intermediary body for several EU funds programs, most notably the IRI grant scheme, which they helped design; (b) many HAMAG-BICRO beneficiaries under th STP II became users of EU-funded IRI grant schemes; (c) UKF helped prepare new research program for ESF funding (managed by the CSF) and steered their beneficiaries to use both ESIF that are managed nationally and highly competitive central European funds for R&D; and (d) TTOs have become central support units to researchers in preparing successful applications for IRI infrastructure program and in managing the EU-funded Centers of Excellence, which include 35 scientific institutions in Croatia through ten Centers. </p>

title.narrative: Prepared set of innovation and R&D policy documents required for absorption of the EU Funds

target.value: Ex ante conditionalities for the use of EU funds for R&D are met ( 3 strategies).

comment.narrative:
<p>Achieved. Indicator was revised through the restructuring in April 2017, to introduce a clarification of the definition.</p>
<p>The three strategies that the project helped formulate are set to strengthen the economy through application of research and innovation. Croatian Roadmap on ESFRI (European Strategy Forum on Research Infrastructures) brought an indicative budget for financing of research infrastructure for the period 2014-2023 and defined priorities regarding national infrastructure and large international projects (projects from the ESFRI and ERIC (European Research Infrastructure Consortium). It included financial obligations and investment plan on an annual basis for 2014-2020, as well as definition of funding sources for concerned ministries (MoSE and MoESD). The Roadmap was updated for coherence with the Smart Specialization Strategy. The project supported the coordination efforts, which enabled that various stakeholders take part in shaping the strategic directions.</p>

actual.value: The Strategy on Education, Science and Technology was adopted by the Parliament in October 2014. The Smart Specialization Strategy has been approved by the European Commission in March 2016. The National Research Infrastructure Roadmap has been updated following the approval of the Smart Specialization Strategy and was adopted.

title.narrative: The share of UKF grants submitted by female applicants (and the share of HAMAG- BICRO's projects submitted) by female applicants)

comment.narrative: <p>Original target was not assigned as STP2 did not have explicit gender goals, but the indicator was intended to allow monitoring the results of the project from a gender perspective (see PAD).</p>
